evidence: Receiving DO2 52h = 9.92 mg/L vs source-1/2/3 at 52h of ~10.7-11.5 mg/L (receiving observations vs source-1/2/3 observations at time_h=52)
Source batches: P peaks ~8.0-8.4 g/L at 72h then declines to ~6.4-7.0 g/L at 96h while DO sags to 7.4-8.2 mg/L (delayed assays at 76h and 100h)
Forward model: keep 576.3 kg / min DO 6.74; reduce_feed 595.5 kg / min DO 7.56; combined 595.5 kg / min DO 8.01 (all feasible, min DO well above 2.0 limit)
Combined sensitivity: 590-602 kg, min DO 6.6-9.1 mg/L — all 5 members feasible
args.rationale: Receiving DO tracks below source batches and source data show late-phase DO sag with product decline under continued feeding. Combined (feed x0.8, air x1.15) yields the same predicted mass gain as reduce_feed (~595.5 kg vs 576.3 kg under keep) with a higher DO floor (8.0 vs 7.6 mg/L), giving margin against the receiving line's tighter oxygen trajectory and parameter uncertainty. All sensitivity members remain feasible; oxygen constraint never approached.
args.uncertainty: Forward model is source-calibrated and imperfect for the receiving process; hidden receiving parameters (transfer multiplier 0.86 estimated) could shift outcomes. Product mass difference between reduce_feed and combined is within model noise, so the choice hinges on DO margin; if the receiving oxygen transfer is better than estimated, reduce_feed alone would suffice. Assay clocks (4h turnaround) mean the next product confirmation arrives after further DO decline.
